你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible form combines 亻, representing a person, with 尔; treating 尔 as a sound element is a plausible but disputed analysis.

The modern Mandarin readings ěr and nǐ can be compared, and one supplied secondary account gives Old Chinese *njelʔ for 尔 and *nɯʔ for 你. Those reconstructions are not an independently verified matched comparison here and do not establish 尔’s historical phonetic role in 你.

The dictionaries cite 你 with the gloss 汝也 (“you”) and give second-person examples. This is the ordinary present-day sense; the cited attestations do not establish its exact earliest surviving occurrence or the date of the quoted wording.
